SOURCE READ. I fetched https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/924 and its PDF (25 pages, the "extended version", PDF dated 2025-07-24) and extracted the full text. It is word-for-word the same version G4 used (verify/p-levels/C4-audit/lit/galbraith2024_eprint924.txt).
- Title: "Climbing and descending tall isogeny volcanos".
- Author: Steven D. Galbraith (University of Auckland), sole author.
- Venue: Research in Number Theory 11, no. 7 (2025). ePrint received 2024-06-10, last revised 2025-07-24.

WHAT THE PAPER STATES (paraphrased, not quoted):
- Theorem 1 (Sec 4)
  - Setup: E0 and E1 over F_q are joined by an F_q-rational isogeny phi of degree N. N > 1000, and N has no prime factor below 4 log N loglog N.
  - Claim: a heuristic algorithm computes a representation of phi that evaluates points in time polynomial in log N. Its expected cost is O~(N^{1/2}) operations in F_q.
  - Inputs: both curves and N are required. Algorithm 1 takes (E0, E1, N).
  - Dimension: the Kani/Robert map F: E0^g x E1^g -> E1^g x E0^g with g in {2,3,4}, so abelian varieties of dimension 4, 6 or 8. The proof uses four squares (g=4): an (M,...,M)-isogeny in dimension 8 with M = N + m = 3^n A_S^2. The two-squares form (dimension 4) is said to be preferred in practice, but m being a sum of two squares is a heuristic. Dimension 2 is never used.
  - Heuristics: Assumption 1 (the i-th Elkies prime is below c + 3 i log i). Sec 2.1 says it can be made rigorous when |D0| is bounded (|D0| < 10^5 via BMO+18). Footnote 5 says ePrint 2025/1243 (with Gilchrist and Robert) removes it. Footnote 8: the meet-in-the-middle is expected to match once. Running times are expected values.
  - Cost structure: about phi(M1) ~ sqrt(N) guesses, each requiring the M1- and M2-isogeny chains to be computed.
- Theorem 2 (Sec 6)
  - Setup: E0 is on the crater (discriminant D0), h0 is the class number of the maximal order (= crater size), and End(E1) has discriminant N^2 D0 with N > log q.
  - Claim: an isogeny E0 -> E1 in heuristic O~(h0 N^{1/2} log(q)^{O(1)}) F_q-operations, by walking the h0 crater curves and applying Theorem 1 to each.
  - The statement omits Theorem 1's small-prime condition on N, even though the proof invokes Theorem 1 with degree N.
  - When h0 = O(1) the cost is O~(q^{1/4}).
- Theorem 4 (Sec 8): Problem B (given only the crater curve and a large prime N dividing the conductor, output the codomain of a descending N-isogeny that can be evaluated) is solvable in O~(q^{1/2}) F_q-operations: guess random curves until one has the right order, then connect them.
- Theorem 5 (Sec 9)
  - Setup: an oracle A solves ECDLP on a fixed positive fraction of curves over F_q with n points.
  - Claim: ECDLP on a RANDOM such curve can be solved with overwhelming probability in O~(q^{2/5}) F_q-operations plus poly(log q) random queries to A.
  - This ignores the negligible set S1 of curves whose conductor is prime to the large primes. For ECC2K-130, S1 is levels 1 and 263, which contain E0, so Theorem 5 says nothing about E0.
- Section 10 (Koblitz-Koblitz-Menezes)
  - Crater to floor: with N > q^{1/4}, the only known ways to move from a crater curve to a floor curve are N^2 > q^{1/2} work or guessing, both at least q^{1/2}. So KKM's "floor may be weaker" speculation is not refuted.
  - Floor to crater: a floor curve can be linked to the crater in at most O(q^{1/4}) when h0 is small, so ECDLP on any given floor curve reduces to the crater.
  - The paper calls its results consistent with KKM.

APPLICATION TO ECC2K-130 (all recomputed):
- The class: t^2 - 4q = -7(263p)^2 and h(-7) = 1, so the crater is {E0}. Kronecker(-7,p) = -1, so level p has p+1 curves, and each is the codomain of a descending F_q-rational p-isogeny from E0.
- Theorem 1 with N = p: p is prime, p > 1000, and p > 581.34 = 4 ln p lnln p. OK.
- Theorem 2: p > log q. OK.
- Following the proof: s = 52 Elkies primes (excluding 263, where Frobenius acts as a scalar), and c = 51 satisfies Assumption 1. Valid (S, A_S, n, m) exist, with m always even and phi(M1) ~ 2^28.0-2^28.4.
- Transfer: the representation (through the adjoint of F) evaluates phi-hat: E1 -> E0. Since gcd(p, N) = 1, the order-N subgroup maps injectively, so ECDLP on a PRESENTED level-p curve reduces to E0.

VERDICT ON THE REDUCTION: yes on paper, with these conditions.
- It is O~(p^{1/2}) = O~(2^28.51) in F_{2^131}-operations. 2^28.5 is only the guess count; each guess costs a full dimension-8 (as proved) or dimension-4 chain of about log2 M1 ~ 29 steps over extension fields.
- The curve must be given explicitly.
- Theorems 1 and 2 are stated as heuristic. The Elkies-prime part is removable for |D0| = 7 (by Sec 2.1's argument; Corollary 1 is stated only for D0 = -3), while the match-uniqueness (footnote 8) and two-squares heuristics remain.
- Level 263p needs a unique ascending 263-step first, because 263 < 687.08 violates Theorem 1.
- The reverse direction (E0 -> a level-p curve) is Problem B: at least q^{1/2} = 2^65.5 per Theorem 4 and Sec 10.

CHARACTERISTIC 2 IS NOT COVERED; it needs components nobody has implemented.
- The paper never discusses characteristic 2. Its only char-related remarks are Lemma 1 (q > 3 prime; used only in Sec 2.2) and the supersingular footnote 6.
- (a) Sec 3 assumes M, #H1 and #H2 are all prime to the characteristic. In Theorem 1, m = M - N is necessarily even when N and M are odd, so the stated hypothesis fails literally in char 2. M is odd, so F is separable. The paper does not say whether this is harmless.
- (b) Algorithm 1, lines 10-11, needs a basis of E[2^2 3^{ceil(n/2)}] (the E1[4] image, following DLRW23 App. F.3, for the meet-in-the-middle test). An ordinary curve in char 2 has cyclic E[4]: I checked that psi_4 of E0 has only 2 distinct roots, so E0[4] = Z/4. No such basis exists, and the step cannot run as written.
- (c) Evaluating the chain relies on LR22/DLRW23 theta models of level 2 or 4. Robert's notes (ePrint 2024/406, on disk) say "Since n = 2 or n = 4 this handle all fields of odd characteristics" and cite char 2 only for dimension 2 ([BCR10b]).
- Needed: a char-2 (l,...,l)-isogeny evaluator in dimension 4 or 8 (for example odd-level theta: 3^g coordinates, and a level coprime to 3 for the 3^n part of M) plus a replacement for the 4-torsion matching check. Nothing on disk implements either.

crux.reasoning:
Short answer: at level p and at level 263p, the effective hardness lies in [60.81, 64.33] (log2 rho iterations). Where it falls depends on one open question: can chains of odd-degree higher-dimensional isogenies be computed in characteristic 2?

Why the p-step is the whole problem:
- Every isogeny from a level-p curve E to E0 has degree divisible by p. It factors through the unique ascending p-isogeny, whose kernel is ker(pi - t/2) inside E[p].
- p is inert in Q(sqrt-7) and divides f, so pi = (t-f)/2 + f*w is congruent to t/2 mod p*O_K. On E0, pi acts on all of E0[p] as the scalar a = t/2 mod p. On E, pi acts on E[p] as a non-semisimple block with eigenvalue a.
- So the kernel points lie over F_{q^r}, r = ord_p(a) = 12208813656794060 (confirmed). Since a^(r/2) = -1, their x-coordinates lie in F_{q^(r/2)}.
- Level 263p adds only a cheap 263-step. Its kernel points are F_q-points of the quadratic twist (263 divides q+1+t), costing about 2^11.4 F_q multiplications. After that the same p-step remains, so both levels get the same interval.

(b) Kernel-point route: infeasible.
- Cofactor multiplication over F_{q^(r/2)} needs at least 2^111.9 F_q multiplications (about 2^120 with realistic arithmetic).
- One field element takes 1.0e17 bytes.
- The kernel polynomial has degree 7.3e16 and takes 1.2e18 bytes.

(c) Modular-polynomial and other classical routes: infeasible.
- Phi_p mod 2 has about 2^113 coefficients. Computing it is O~(p^2) with Kunzweiler-Robert (itself a higher-dimensional method) or O~(p^3) ≈ 2^171 with the CRT methods.
- Phi_p(1,Y) mod 2 equals H_{-7p^2} mod 2; the CM method for that costs about 2^116.9.
- The Couveignes, Lercier and De Feo characteristic-2 algorithms are at least O~(p^2) ≈ 2^114.
- Caruso-Eid-Lercier (JLMS 2021) computes characteristic-2 isogenies in O~(l). But it needs the isogeny differential c, which their Section 3.2 obtains only for horizontal isogenies from class-group relations. For this vertical isogeny, c is a 2-adic unit that no known method determines. Even with c known, the model gives about 2^73 F_q multiplications, which is above break-even.
- Break-even: transport plus E0 rho beats native rho only if the transport costs less than 2^66.5 to 2^67.2 F_q multiplications.

(a) Kani / higher-dimensional route: the only one that can beat native rho.
- Galbraith 2024/924 and Galbraith-Gilchrist-Robert 2025/1243 guess the unknown isogeny's action on smooth M-torsion, one unit of fixed norm per prime (l - chi(l) choices), about sqrt(p) guesses in total. GGR's self-pairing gain here comes only from m = 7, a factor of sqrt(7).
- Characteristic 2 changes two things:
  1. 2-power torsion is unusable. E[2^e] is Z/2^e times mu_{2^e}, so the Kani kernel contains a non-reduced part. The étale half also needs the field F_{q^(2^(e-2))} (checked: v_2(#E0(F_{q^k})) = 2 + v_2(k)). Richelot and theta (2,2)-chains therefore do not apply.
  2. Only odd l can be used. The fields of definition are u(3)=8, u(5)=24, u(11)=10, u(23)=11 and u(263)=2. The product of usable primes with u ≤ 64 is 2^48.
- Every published algorithm for such isogeny chains assumes odd characteristic (see the literature check below).
- Robert's survey (2024/1071, footnote 10) says p = 2 can be handled by the lift-and-reduce technique of Gaudry-Lubicz 2009. It also says AVIsogenies contains dimension-2 isogeny code for characteristic 2. No characteristic-2 Kani pipeline (gluing from E x E0, splitting) is published.
- Concrete parameters exist:
  - Dimension 2, meet-in-the-middle with stored lists: M = p + b^2 smooth. 4441 such M were found for even b < 2^28 and primes up to 5000. The best is b = 251885052, lists of 2^27.4 and 2^30.4. Modelled cost 2^52.5 times kappa F_q multiplications.
  - Dimension 4 (M - p a sum of two squares), single loop: M = 3^2*(5*11*23*29*53*67)^2 with 2^28.9 guesses. Cost 2^55.5 times kappa.
  - Dimension 8 (four squares, Galbraith's Theorem 1 as written) is never competitive: at least 2^78 in this model, and at least 2^70 even with l^8 constants.

What the endpoints depend on:
- Lower endpoint 60.81 (E0 rho with the tau speed-up): reached to within 0.1 bit if a characteristic-2 Kani pipeline exists with overhead kappa up to about 2^7 in dimension 2, or up to about 2^4 in dimension 4. That is the case for direct characteristic-2 formulas in the Gaudry-Lubicz style (kappa ≤ 2^2), which give 60.81 to 60.84.
- In between: running the computation 2-adically (lift-and-reduce at run time, kappa about 2^7.5 to 2^11) gives 60.9 to 62.0 in dimension 2, and 61.5 to 64.3 in dimension 4.
- Upper endpoint 64.33: native rho with the negation map only. On E(F_q), pi is the identity, and Frobenius conjugates give no class reduction. This applies if no characteristic-2 algorithm for these isogeny chains exists, because every non-Kani route costs at least 2^73 F_q multiplications (above break-even).
- The model constants are uncertain by a few bits; kappa absorbs them.

Two of the three parts hold as stated. The third holds in direction, but its cost figure is too high.

(1) Construction. No structural route is cheaper than generic search. I derived algebraically that (pi-c)/p lies in Z + 263 O_K, with c = t/2 mod p. So pi acts as the scalar c on E[p] for E0 and for all 262 floor curves. Two things follow: all p+1 order-p subgroups are F_q-rational, and every nonzero p-torsion point lives exactly over F_{q^r}. Nothing smaller exists over any F_{2^m}, because the smallest m with tau^m = +-1 is 131·r/2.

Each route fails for a concrete reason:
- **Other levels:** any isogeny from level 1 or 263 into level p or 263p has p dividing its degree, so the same kernel obstruction applies.
- **Higher-dimensional (Kani) isogenies:** they need p | degree whenever T_p is an O_K-module. And because p is inert, no endomorphism of E0 cuts out a single order-p subgroup.
- **Descending kernel:** one F_{q^(r/2)} element is 2^59.47 bits, and sqrt-Velu costs at least 2^80.95 F_q-mults.
- **CM:** |D| = 2^116.85, and even Phi_p(1,Y) mod 2 is 16.3 PiB.
- **Lifting:** the canonical lift is unramified, and a char-0 j-value has degree p+1.
- **Literature:** Galbraith 2024 §8/§10 knows only "N^2 work or guessing". GGR 2025 (ePrint 2025/1243) says descending costs O~(l^2) and recommends reconstructing the ascending dual instead, which needs the target curve.

The "≥ 2^72.97 F_q-mults" figure is not a lower bound, though:
- **mod 16:** bit_3(#E) = 1 + sigma_2(b), where sigma_2 is the second coefficient of b's characteristic polynomial over F_2. This is a quadratic form. It checked out on F_2^131 (1000/1000 and 1500/1500).
- **mod 32 and mod 64:** bits 4 and 5 are functions of sigma_2..sigma_8, again 1500/1500 on F_2^131. Their Boolean degree is at most 5 and 9. The fast Gray-code enumeration method (FES) evaluates them in O(degree) bit operations per candidate.
- **Result:** these filters cut the number of ladders by 2^3 at almost no cost.
- **Modular families:** a twisted X_1(11) family (genus 1) raises the hit rate by 10; the measured share on F_2^131 is 0.0992 against 0.1000 predicted. The ~100 F_q-mults per sample is my estimate; I did not implement or time the family. Families pinning the class residue mod 3, 5 or 7 give smaller gains. Combining families already reaches genus 7 (level 21) or 29 (level 35), so they cannot be stacked cheaply.
- **Best found:** about 2^70.0 to 2^71.3 F_q-mults, which is 2^6.8 to 2^8.2 E0 rho solves.
- **Why E0 rho is still out of reach:** matching it would need 2^9.84 fewer ladders with at most 0.29 F_q-mults of pre-ladder work per candidate. Only about 3 (possibly 4) 2-adic bits are that cheap.

So the conclusion stands in weaker form. Building a level-p curve costs about 100× or more an ECC2K-130 break. It also costs more than solving natively on that curve afterwards (2^66.65).

(2) Lower endpoint. 60.809 is right as a best-known-attack floor:
- tau, the norm-2 element, exists only at conductor 1.
- The smallest non-scalar endomorphism has degree 2^114.85 at level p and 2^130.93 at level 263p.
- No level-p curve has j in F_2, so none has an F_2-Frobenius endomorphism.
- GHS gives m = 131 for every b with Tr(b)=1 except b=1.
- The embedding degree 2^117.38 and the twist order are the same for every curve in the class.

It is not backed by a reduction, however. E0 → level p is Galbraith's Problem B, which costs at least as much as construction. So a level-p-specific weakness would not contradict E0's hardness; this is the KKM speculation, discussed in Galbraith 2024 §10. The endpoint is attained only if transport is free.

(3) Upper endpoint. log2 sqrt(pi·N/4) = 64.3257, which is E0's 60.8090 plus log2 sqrt(131) = 3.5167. It is correct as an ideal upper bound. The 131 conjugate curves E'^(2^k) are distinct, so sigma^k merges no points and gives no rho speed-up.
